proposals.before: Wang Zhengyan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Revenue; Cui Xie, censor-in-chief, was made Minister of Rites; Cui Jujian, Vice Minister of Punishments, History Office compiler, and acting institute director, was made censor-in-chief; and Gui Ai, Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
proposals.after: Wang Zhengyan, Minister of Rites, was made Minister of Revenue; Cui Xie, censor-in-chief, was made Minister of Rites; Cui Jujian, Vice Minister of Punishments, History Office compiler, and acting institute director, was made censor-in-chief; and Gui Ai, Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was made Vice Minister of Punishments.
proposals.reason: 尚書左丞 is a Department of State Affairs office, not a Secretariat post; the English office name is wrong.

proposals.before: Minister of Rites Wang Zhengyan was made Minister of Revenue; censor-in-chief Cui Xie was made Minister of Rites; Punishments vice minister, History Office compiler, and acting institute director Cui Jujian was made censor-in-chief; Left Assistant Minister of the Secretariat Gui Ai was made Punishments vice minister.
proposals.after: Minister of Rites Wang Zhengyan was made Minister of Revenue; censor-in-chief Cui Xie was made Minister of Rites; Punishments vice minister, History Office compiler, and acting institute director Cui Jujian was made censor-in-chief; Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs Gui Ai was made Punishments vice minister.
proposals.reason: 尚書左丞 belongs to the Shangshu, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: Li Guangxu became Right Secretariat assistant minister.
proposals.after: Li Guangxu became Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書右丞 is not a Secretariat office; the English title is mistranslated.

proposals.before: Presentation Attendant Li Guangxu was made Right Assistant Minister of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: Presentation Attendant Li Guangxu was made Right Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs.
proposals.reason: 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat.

proposals.before: On jichou Li Shaopeng of Xiang and Dong Zhang of Bin became their circuits' commissioners.
proposals.after: On jichou Li Shaogong of Xiang and Dong Zhang of Bin became their circuits' commissioners.
proposals.reason: 珙 is gong, not peng; Li Shaopeng mistransliterates 李紹珙.

proposals.before: On jichou Xiangzhou acting regent Li Shaopeng was made Xiangzhou military commissioner, and Binzhou acting regent Dong Zhang was made Binzhou military commissioner.
proposals.after: On jichou Xiangzhou acting regent Li Shaogong was made Xiangzhou military commissioner, and Binzhou acting regent Dong Zhang was made Binzhou military commissioner.
proposals.reason: 珙 should be romanized Shaogong, not Shaopeng.

proposals.before: On guisi the Secretariat ordered the dowager's posthumous evaluation read in Taizu's chamber with ranked officials from the two departments, Censorate, Secretariat, and ministries present."
proposals.after: On guisi the Secretariat memorialized that the late Empress Dowager's posthumous evaluation should be read in Taizu's chamber of the Imperial Temple, and that day officials of the fifth rank and above from the two departments and the Censorate, the fourth rank and above from the Department of State Affairs, and the third rank and above from the various offices should line up in order at the Imperial Temple.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English wrongly turns a memorial (上言) into an order, garbles the three distinct rank thresholds, and leaves a stray closing quotation mark.

proposals.before: On guisi the Secretariat memorialized: "The late Empress Dowager's posthumous evaluation should be read in the Imperial Temple's Taizu chamber; that day let officials of the third rank and above from the two departments, the Censorate, and the fifth rank and above from the Secretariat, and third rank and above from the various offices, line up in order at the Imperial Temple."
proposals.after: On guisi the Secretariat memorialized: "The late Empress Dowager's posthumous evaluation should be read in the Imperial Temple's Taizu chamber; that day let officials of the fifth rank and above from the two departments and the Censorate, the fourth rank and above from the Department of State Affairs, and the third rank and above from the various offices, line up in order at the Imperial Temple."
proposals.reason: Literal English misassigns the rank cutoffs: 两省御史台 are fifth and above, 尚书省 fourth and above, and 诸司 third and above.

proposals.before: When I lately swept Liang like wind and lightning, I restored the ancestral temple and Tang's mid-restoration reign.
proposals.after: When I lately drove sharp hosts like the wind and swept the wicked like lightning, I restored the fallen ancestral temple and continued the mid-restoration calendar.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English invents 'Liang', which is not present in the Chinese 风驱锐旅，电扫凶渠.

proposals.before: Ren Yuan of Works and Hanlin Li Yu joined Jiji's staff.
proposals.after: Ren Huan of Works and Hanlin Li Yu joined Jiji's staff.
proposals.reason: 任圜 is Ren Huan; 'Yuan' is a mistranscription of the personal name.

proposals.before: An edict ordered Minister of Works Ren Yuan and Hanlin academician Li Yu to join the Prince of Wei's military council.
proposals.after: An edict ordered Minister of Works Ren Huan and Hanlin academician Li Yu to join the Prince of Wei's military council.
proposals.reason: 任圜 should be romanized Ren Huan, not Ren Yuan.

proposals.before: On wusi the Secretariat asked to name the dowager's tomb Kunling."
proposals.after: On jisi the Secretariat asked to name the dowager's tomb Kunling.
proposals.reason: Chinese 己巳 is jisi, not wusi; remove the stray trailing quote.

proposals.before: On wusi the Secretariat memorialized: "We ask that Empress Dowager Zhenjian's tomb be named Kunling."
proposals.after: On jisi the Secretariat memorialized: "We ask that Empress Dowager Zhenjian's tomb be named Kunling."
proposals.reason: Chinese 己巳 corresponds to jisi; wusi misreads the sexagenary day.

proposals.before: Tribes along the road plundered them; cold and hunger killed multitudes; barely a hundred reached Shu, and only he, Tian Zongmin, and a few others got through.
proposals.after: Tribes along the road plundered them; cold and hunger killed multitudes; barely a hundred reached Shu, and only he, Tian Zongrui, and a few others got through.
proposals.reason: Chinese 田宗汭 uses 汭 (ruì); Zongmin does not match the given name.

proposals.before: Along the way western tribes plundered them; freezing and hunger trampled one another to death; by the time they reached Shu barely more than a hundred survived, and only he with Tian Zongmin and a few others escaped through alive.
proposals.after: Along the way western tribes plundered them; freezing and hunger trampled one another to death; by the time they reached Shu barely more than a hundred survived, and only he with Tian Zongrui and a few others escaped through alive.
proposals.reason: Chinese 汭 is ruì; Tian Zongmin mistransliterates 田宗汭.

proposals.before: On the gengshen new moon of the tenth month ministers and officials of the third rank and above named the dowager Empress Zhenjian at Changshou Palace.
proposals.after: On the gengshen new moon of the tenth month, ministers and officials of the third rank and above went to Changshou Palace and presented the late Empress Dowager's posthumous title as Empress Dowager Zhenjian.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic omits going to the palace and that 諡 is a posthumous title for the late (大行) empress dowager.

proposals.before: At first Cunxu wanted her beside Li Keyong's tomb at Daizhou; debate said the Son of Heaven should not split his home north and south."
proposals.after: At first the Emperor wished to bury her beside the Martial Emperor's tomb at Daizhou; memorial debate said: "The Son of Heaven takes the four seas as his home and should not divide north and south."
proposals.reason: Stray closing quote and incomplete memorial quotation; 帝/武皇 are Emperor/Martial Emperor in the Chinese.

proposals.before: On gengxu, the Emperor's younger brother Yanzhou military commissioner Cunba, Hua prefecture military commissioner Cunwo, Left Golden Spear Guard senior general and Jinzhou military commissioner Cunyi, and Xingzhou military commissioner Cunji were all appointed recalled-from-mourning Cloud Banner generals and Right Golden Spear Guard senior generals of the same rank.
proposals.after: On gengxu, the Emperor's younger brother Yunzhou military commissioner Cunba, Hua prefecture military commissioner Cunwo, Left Golden Wu Guard senior general and Jinzhou military commissioner Cunyi, and Xingzhou military commissioner Cunji were all appointed recalled-from-mourning Cloud Banner generals and Right Golden Wu Guard senior generals of the same rank.
proposals.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou (兗州); 金吾 is the Golden Wu / Imperial Insignia Guard, not Golden Spear Guard.

proposals.before: Jingnan commissioner Gao Jixing reported recovering Gui, Qi, and Zhong.
proposals.after: Jingnan commissioner Gao Jixing reported recovering Gui, Kui, and Zhong.
proposals.reason: 夔 is Kui, not Qi; the prefecture triad is 歸、夔、忠.

proposals.before: Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jixing memorialized that he had recovered Gui, Qi, and Zhong prefectures.
proposals.after: Jingnan military commissioner Gao Jixing memorialized that he had recovered Gui, Kui, and Zhong prefectures.
proposals.reason: 夔 is Kui, not Qi; matches 歸、夔、忠.

proposals.before: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, Secretariat director Li Zhou, Ouyang Huang, and others had plotted against the ruler and were already beheaded and displayed.
proposals.after: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu and Ouyang Huang, alike had plotted, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.
proposals.reason: Chinese 宣徽使李周輅歐陽晃 names Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu (李周輅) and Ouyang Huang; Secretariat director Li Zhou mistranslates office and personal name.

proposals.before: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi, Jing Runcheng, and Director of the Palace Secretariat Li Zhou, Ouyang Huang, and others alike harbored divergent plots, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.
proposals.after: he also reported that Shu privy commissioners Song Guangsi and Jing Runcheng, and Xuanhui commissioners Li Zhoulu and Ouyang Huang, alike harbored divergent plots, confused the Shu ruler, and had already been beheaded and displayed.
proposals.reason: 宣徽使 is Xuanhui commissioner, not Director of the Palace Secretariat; 李周輅 is the single name Li Zhoulu with 歐陽晃 under that office.

proposals.before: Li Lingde of Tong—acting Grand Guardian and chancellor—became Sui commissioner;
proposals.after: Li Lingde of Tong—acting Grand Guardian and chancellor—became Suizhou commissioner;
proposals.reason: Chinese 遂州 is Suizhou; idiomatic 'Sui' wrongly shortens the prefecture and risks confusion with another Sui.

proposals.before: On bingxu third aunt Song was made Princess of Great Righteousness and Tranquility, elder sister Meng Princess of Jade Splendor, and eleventh sister Zhang Princess of Jade Blossom.
proposals.after: On bingxu the third aunt of the Song clan was made Grand Princess of Yining, the elder sister of the Meng clan Princess of Qionghua, and the eleventh younger sister of the Zhang clan Princess of Yaoying.
proposals.reason: 義寧/瓊華/瑤英 are proper title-fief names, not free English glosses; 大長公主 is Grand Princess.

proposals.before: On bingxu, the third aunt the Song clan was enfeoffed Princess of Great Righteousness and Tranquility; the elder sister the Meng clan Princess of Jade Splendor; the eleventh younger sister the Zhang clan Princess of Jade Blossom.
proposals.after: On bingxu, the third aunt of the Song clan was enfeoffed Grand Princess of Yining; the elder sister of the Meng clan, Princess of Qionghua; the eleventh younger sister of the Zhang clan, Princess of Yaoying.
proposals.reason: Same proper-name error as the idiomatic field: place/title names should not be semanticized.

proposals.before: On yisi Li Cuny of Jin became Yan commissioner and Li Cunque of Xiang became Jin commissioner.
proposals.after: On yisi Li Cunyi of Jin became Fu commissioner and Li Cunque of Xiang became Jin commissioner.
proposals.reason: 李存乂 is Cunyi, not Cuny; 鄜州 is Fu, not Yan.

proposals.before: On yisi, Jinzhou military commissioner Li Cuny was made Yanzhou military commissioner, and Xiangzhou prefect Li Cunque was made Jinzhou military commissioner.
proposals.after: On yisi, Jinzhou military commissioner Li Cunyi was made Fuzhou military commissioner, and Xiangzhou prefect Li Cunque was made Jinzhou military commissioner.
proposals.reason: 李存乂 is Cunyi; 鄜州 is Fuzhou (Fu), not Yanzhou.

proposals.before: On xinhai an investiture edict enfeoffed Cunba as Prince Yong, Cunmei as Prince Yong, Cunwo as Prince Shen, Cunyi as Prince Mu, Cunque as Prince Tong, and Cunji as Prince Ya.
proposals.after: On xinhai an investiture edict enfeoffed Cunba as Prince Yong (永), Cunmei as Prince Yong (邕), Cunwo as Prince Shen, Cunyi as Prince Mu, Cunque as Prince Tong, and Cunji as Prince Ya.
proposals.reason: 第三弟存美 was enfeoffed 邕王, not a second 永王; English must distinguish 永王 from 邕王.

proposals.before: On xinhai, an investiture edict made the Emperor's second younger brother Cunba able to be enfeoffed Prince Yong, the third younger brother Cunmei able to be enfeoffed Prince Yong, the fourth younger brother Cunwo able to be enfeoffed Prince Shen, the fifth younger brother Cunyi able to be enfeoffed Prince Mu, the sixth younger brother Cunque able to be enfeoffed Prince Tong, and the seventh younger brother Cunji able to be enfeoffed Prince Ya.
proposals.after: On xinhai, an investiture edict made the Emperor's second younger brother Cunba able to be enfeoffed Prince Yong (永), the third younger brother Cunmei able to be enfeoffed Prince Yong (邕), the fourth younger brother Cunwo able to be enfeoffed Prince Shen, the fifth younger brother Cunyi able to be enfeoffed Prince Mu, the sixth younger brother Cunque able to be enfeoffed Prince Tong, and the seventh younger brother Cunji able to be enfeoffed Prince Ya.
proposals.reason: Chinese 邕王 for Cunmei was mistranslated as the same Prince Yong as 永王.

Literal likewise mislabels 尚書左丞 as a Secretariat post; Department of State Affairs is correct.
Chinese 尚書右丞 belongs to the Department of State Affairs, not the Secretariat; the proposed title matches.

decisions.reason: Chinese uses 帝 and 武皇 with a full 奏議 quotation; the after restores those labels and fixes the stray quote.

decisions.reason: 鄆州 is Yunzhou, not Yanzhou, and 金吾 is the Golden Wu Guard, not Golden Spear.
